title: unera
intro: Brand identity and stationery for an educational social network start-up entering a crowded online-learning market. Five letters, five shapes, and a palette everyone can read.
brief: unera needed to stand out in a saturated online-education market and arrive with a confident, noticeable presence. The look had to be minimal and clean but still memorable and approachable: contemporary, yet relatable to an older audience, youthful and inspiring, and clearly separate from the big corporations. The palette came with a firm requirement too: it had to work for people with colour blindness. And because the company planned to brand its correspondence heavily, the identity had to hold up in print and at exhibitions as well as on screen.
did: Developed together with Monica Ramilison. We reduced each letter of the name to a simple geometric form: a square, a circle, a notched circle, a triangle and a rounded half-shape. Set in a row, they spell out the wordmark; stacked into a square, they become a compact monogram; repeated, they build a pattern that can fill a poster or a letterhead. One small set of shapes ends up doing the work of the whole system.

The colours, a muted plum, lilac, coral, soft yellow and light grey, were chosen so that each stays distinct across every type of colour blindness, which keeps the shapes readable for everyone and gives the brand a warmth that feels far from corporate. From there we set up the core stationery, business cards and letterheads, so the brand was ready for the heavy correspondence the company had planned.
coverAlt: Poster mockup for unera on a yellow background: the geometric monogram and wordmark above a pattern of colourful squares, circles and triangles
